business_problem: Shihuo needed a more accurate and scalable way to match its product catalog against listings across many external commerce channels so users could compare prices and buy the right items. Its earlier approach of full-text retrieval plus manual review could not keep up with long-tail SKU growth, and the self-managed Milvus cluster it tried next introduced instability, higher operations complexity, and extra infrastructure work.
solution_summary: Shihuo redesigned its commerce-matching pipeline around Alibaba Cloud Vector Search Service Milvus Edition and PAI-EAS. For hot products, the business can still preserve precise human curation, but at long-tail scale the platform now combines full-text retrieval, vector recall, and manual verification. Product data and cross-channel catalog signals are embedded with model services exposed through PAI-EAS, then stored in the managed Milvus service as the low-latency similarity-search layer that powers product association in the app. Moving from self-built Milvus to the managed service also gave Shihuo built-in monitoring, alerting, smoother capacity changes, and more predictable runtime behavior under sustained writes. The result is a retrieval architecture that improves matching quality for shopping decisions while keeping the vector platform much easier to operate as SKU counts and cross-channel comparisons continue to grow.

solution_components.name: Vector Search Service Milvus Edition
solution_components.role: Stores product vectors and returns low-latency similarity matches for cross-channel product association.

solution_components.name: PAI-EAS
solution_components.role: Runs the embedding-model training and inference services used to generate vectors for retrieval.

data_flow: Product records from Shihuo and external sales channels are converted into embeddings through PAI-EAS, written into the managed Milvus vector index, and then combined with full-text retrieval and human review to identify the correct cross-channel product matches shown in the app.
business_outcome: Shihuo improved product-association quality for long-tail commerce data while gaining a far more stable and supportable vector stack. Managed Milvus lifted QPS by around 10% in testing, kept CPU utilization stable near 50% at 2K TPS writes, and eliminated a large share of the hidden people cost that a self-operated vector cluster would have required.
metrics: self-managing the cluster would have required more than one-third of operations manpower
architecture_clues: The final retrieval path combines vector recall, full-text retrieval, and manual review rather than replacing all logic with embeddings.
PAI-EAS is used as the model online service for embedding-related training and inference tasks.
Milvus is consumed as a fully managed cloud-native service with built-in monitoring and smoother scaling controls.
The platform preserves human curation for hot products while using vectors to scale long-tail catalog coverage.
